title: TimeMixer seasonal-timescale Mirror address bank
hypothesis: On two pinned time-series domains with different dominant periods, a low-description timescale×regime coordinate bank over one shared multiscale mixer reduces macro audit MASE by at least 2% relative to hard-shared TimeMixer and beats matched additive scale/regime coefficients at equal byte cost.
physical_object: One shared multiscale mixer forecast backbone
mirror_coordinate: factorized learned scale and regime coordinates for shared mixing coefficients
logical_multiplicity: Regime-conditioned predictors across multiple temporal scales

dataset_selection.development_source: ETTh1 and ETTm1 from zhouhaoyi/ETDataset main commit resolved by GitHub API at protocol-freeze time; listed variables HUFL,HULL,MUFL,MULL,LUFL,LULL,OT
dataset_selection.fresh_source: PEMS-BAY excluded to preserve freshness relative to MA-1048; use final 20% temporal windows of each pinned ETT dataset as fresh audit, after development selection on first 60%/middle 20%
dataset_selection.split: chronological official ETT train/validation/test boundaries are avoided in favor of contiguous 60/20/20; context 96 and horizon 24
dataset_selection.windows: deterministically select max 48 training origins per series, 12 development origins, and 12 audit origins from the corresponding split; M and S variants share same procedure
dataset_selection.note: MA-1046/1047 used ETT, so audit windows are not program-level fresh. This is clearly scoped single-run fresh time split only; no claim of new data source.

model.implementation: Official TimeMixer source models/TimeMixer.py from thuml/Time-Series-Library commit 4e938a1767106324dd753b2a44832bf870a0252e; port only needed multiscale mixing components into adapter to avoid unrelated framework dependency
model.training: Small CPU model, same update budget and data order for all variants; 20 epochs maximum, AdamW, batch 64; lock after development selection and before final-20% audit

development.selection_metric: macro MASE across development series and horizons

success_gate: At least 2% lower macro audit MASE than hard sharing and the byte-matched additive control, with complete payload smaller than independent per-domain models.
failure_gate: No audit quality gain over hard sharing, or additive control matches/beats Mirror at comparable bytes.
boundaries: fixed-budget screen is not capacity claim
ETT data source was used in prior MA-1046/1047; audit uses unseen temporal windows but not a new dataset
CPU-scale adapter is not an official benchmark reproduction
no GPU/runtime generalization from CPU timings
